mechanism.validator_requirement: set(traces_by_field) must equal {observations[i] for each observation} ∪ {candidate_promise_texts[j] for each promise}
mechanism.model_behaviour: traces every observation, never traces any candidate promise
mechanism.prompt_instruction_verbatim_v1: Every observation and candidate promise needs a source_trace entry.
mechanism.prompt_instruction_verbatim_v2: Every observation and candidate promise needs a source_trace entry. Emit one source_trace entry per observation and one per candidate promise; a single entry never covers two fields.
why_the_model_misses_it: v1: the instruction was abstract and never named the exact field strings observations[N] / candidate_promise_texts[M];
v1: the phrase 'an entry' was singular, matching a one-per-existing-observation reading;
v1: the schema example showed a single literal field value, from which whole-collection coverage cannot be inferred;
v2: even the explicit 'one per candidate promise; a single entry never covers two fields' wording, plus a candidate_promise_texts[0] example, is followed only about one third of the time;

root behavioural tendency confirmed across every real call: the model treats an observation that quotes the same AGENT sentence as already covering that promise, so it emits exactly one trace per observation (4obs+2prom -> 4 traces under v1; 3obs+1prom -> 3 traces under v2).

prompt_variant_reliability_probe.recommended_prompt_increment_verbatim:
Worked example. If the source text contains exactly one AGENT message that makes a promise, and you produce:

  "observations": ["a", "b", "c"],
  "candidate_promise_texts": ["the promise"]

then source_trace MUST contain exactly four entries, one per element:

  "source_trace": [
    {"field": "observations[0]",            "source_type": "IMAGE", "source_id": "<id>"},
    {"field": "observations[1]",            "source_type": "IMAGE", "source_id": "<id>"},
    {"field": "observations[2]",            "source_type": "CHAT",  "source_id": "<id>"},
    {"field": "candidate_promise_texts[0]", "source_type": "CHAT",  "source_id": "<id>"}
  ]

The fourth entry is required even when observations[2] already quotes the same agent sentence. An observation trace never satisfies the promise trace.
prompt_variant_reliability_probe.conclusion: the v2 change alone does NOT close the gap; adding the worked example does, and it preserves the image traces that variant C loses

criterion_1_real_chat_plus_image_to_extr.repeatability_caveat: CRITICAL — see prompt_variant_reliability_probe. The pass was produced by the tool's --attempts 2 loop: attempt 1 was rejected with MISSING_FIELD_TRACE and attempt 2 was accepted. Under prompt v2 the model emits the required promise trace only about one third of the time (measured 1/3), so this criterion is NOT stably achieved by the current prompt.

criterion_3_twenty_second_budget.measurement_defect: see second_defect below — the tool sums every attempt into model_bound_ms, so two ~10 s calls exceeded the 20 s verdict even though no single request did. Under v2 the two calls were ~6.4 s each and the sum stayed inside the budget, so the defect did not trigger this time, but it remains latency-dependent and unfixed.

second_defect_journey_path_always_raised.symptom: AttributeError: type object 'AnalyzeService' has no attribute '_compile_from_server_facts'
second_defect_journey_path_always_raised.why_it_is_a_bug: backend/src/covenia_b/services/analyze.py (git status clean, modified by nobody) defines _DEFAULT_POLICY at line 72, _compile_from_server_facts at line 399, _enrich_extracted_journey at line 410 and _aggregate_server_evidence at line 539 as MODULE-LEVEL objects. Only _validate_candidate (lines 321-327) is really an AnalyzeService @staticmethod. The tool therefore crashed on every run that reached journey construction.
second_defect_journey_path_always_raised.why_it_hid_until_now: under prompt v1 the candidate was rejected at source validation, so the run never reached the journey projection and the latent AttributeError was never triggered. The previous round's report described extracted_journey as NOT_REACHED, which was true, but the code path had in fact never been executed.
second_defect_journey_path_always_raised.aggravating_factor: the crash escaped the tool's exception handling, so NO artifact was written at all. A genuine defect therefore looked like a missing run, and the v2 probe produced no evidence until this was fixed.
fix_applied: import the four module-level objects in _load_modules() and resolve them through the modules mapping
update the three call sites to use the module-level helpers instead of attributes of AnalyzeService

add a catch-all `except Exception` handler in main() that writes the failure document first and then re-raises, so an unanticipated exception can never again be silent and the tool never converts a crash into a verdict

verification_after_fix._load_modules_resolution: all four objects resolve (DEFAULT_POLICY=CommitmentPolicy, compile_from_server_facts, enrich_extracted_journey, aggregate_server_evidence)
verification_after_fix.end_to_end: the pytest live marker run then reached journey construction and produced a full PASS
